## Appearance

Marilla Cuthbert is a tall, thin, and gaunt woman characterized by sharp angles rather than curves. She has sallow cheeks and dark hair streaked with gray, which she wears tightly twisted into a hard knot at the back of her head secured by two aggressive wire hairpins. At times, she bears a tired appearance, with hair that has grown grayer over the years.

## Personality

A self-contained and sensible woman of narrow experience, Marilla Cuthbert possesses a rigid conscience and a strict, critical disposition. She holds strong convictions regarding child-rearing, detesting stinginess in children and firmly believing that a moral lesson should accompany every remark made to them. Though reserved in expressing her affection and inexorable when setting expectations, she eventually mellows over time. She takes pride in her domestic duties, being determined not to be eclipsed by other local housekeepers, and is celebrated for making yellow plum preserves and three-year-old homemade currant wine. Driven by a sense of duty, she commits herself fully to raising [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), aiming to teach her cooking and drill her into a tranquil uniformity of disposition.

## History

Living at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), Marilla Cuthbert had enjoyed a quiet life with her brother [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md), though she had once suffered from low self-esteem as a child after being called homely. She had also previously been close with John Blythe, but broke off their relationship after refusing to forgive him following a quarrel. Marilla and [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) decided to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, but a mix-up resulted in a young girl, [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), being brought to them instead. Though initially determined to send [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) back to the asylum, Marilla relented after visiting Mrs. [Spencer](../character/spencer.md) and learning of a local woman's harsh plan for the child. She resolved to keep [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), taking on the responsibility of raising her despite having no prior experience with children.

Over time, Marilla found herself growing deeply fond of [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) despite the girl's frequent misadventures, such as accidentally serving currant wine to a friend, dyeing her hair green, or mistakenly flavoring a cake with liniment. When Marilla falsely accused [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) of losing her inherited amethyst brooch, she was forced to admit her error and apologize after discovering the pin snagged in her own shawl. Though often stern, Marilla consistently supported Anne's growth, agreeing to enroll her in advanced classes to prepare for the Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#academy) entrance examinations. After [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) passed away suddenly following a bank failure, Marilla learned from an oculist that her own eyesight was failing, leaving her considering the sale of [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) promptly gave up her college scholarship to stay in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), teach, and care for Marilla, securing their home and future together.

## Quotes

> "I’d never dream of taking a girl to bring up. I wonder at Mrs. Alexander Spencer for doing it. But there, she wouldn’t shrink from adopting a whole orphan asylum if she took it into her head."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P29](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0029)

> “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VI. Marilla Makes Up Her Mind P35](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0035)

> "I suppose we could, but we decided not to. Matthew took a fancy to her. And I must say I like her myself—although I admit she has her faults. The house seems a different place already. She’s a real bright little thing."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P9](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0009)

> "when I make up my mind to do a thing it stays made up. I suppose you’d like to see Anne. I’ll call her in."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P12](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0012)

> "I’m not trying to excuse her. She’s been very naughty and I’ll have to give her a talking to about it. But we must make allowances for her. She’s never been taught what is right. And you were too hard on her, Rachel."
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER IX. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Properly Horrified P28](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0028)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla initially intends to send [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) back to the asylum after a mix-up brings a young girl to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) instead of the expected boy. However, after hearing Anne's harsh life story and seeing an unpleasant alternative home offered by Mrs. [Blewett](../character/peter-blewett.md), Marilla pities [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and agrees with [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) to adopt her. As Anne's adoptive mother, Marilla works to instill practical skills, proper religious manners, and discipline in her, though Anne's vivid imagination often distracts her from her lessons.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P1](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P8](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0008), [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P39](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0039), +20 more_

### [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/marilla-cuthbert--rachel-lynde.md)

Marilla maintains a longstanding friendship with Mrs. Rachel [Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) despite their differing opinions. Mrs. Rachel is comfortable speaking her mind, such as strongly disapproving of the [Cuthberts](../codex/factions.md#cuthberts) adopting an orphan and later insulting Anne's looks, which sparks a dramatic conflict between [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and Mrs. Rachel. Despite these clashes, Marilla trusts her judgment enough to consult her for parenting advice when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) refuses to attend school.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P3](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P5](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0005), [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P12](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0012), +13 more_
